clue.text: Minor investors' allotments?

parts.note: people with few shares own modest stakes in a company; read differently, the phrase describes little plots of farmland

explanation.surface: A question about how shares are parcelled out to people with only a little money to invest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Allotments' suggests share issues; the answer is literal land: small plots worked by a single family.
explanation.definitionFit: Small plots of farmland are the land a modest grower holds, punning on a small investor's modest share stakes.

clue.text: Second injured heron or other waterbird

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a very short time, as is a second

indicators.note: something injured is damaged and bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heron has been hurt, along with some other bird of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal; it is a brief moment, and 'or' only joins the heron to the bird defined.
explanation.definitionFit: A moorhen is a small dark rail of ponds and rivers, a waterbird other than the heron named in the clue.

clue.text: Placed a cover outside

indicators.note: the cover goes outside, so its letters wrap round the other piece

parts.note: a lid is a cover for a pot or box

explanation.surface: Someone put a covering round the outside of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are past tenses meaning set down or put in position, simple synonyms.

clue.text: Afternoon meal that's served by airlines

definitions.meaning: a late-afternoon spread with a cooked dish, bread and cakes, in Britain
taken literally, tea served up in the sky, at altitude, by an aircraft crew

explanation.surface: A description of the late-afternoon snack offered on a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: tea poured at altitude is tea served aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a substantial early-evening or late-afternoon meal with tea is traditionally called by this name.

clue.text: Making sense of Gallico?

indicators.note: making sense of a jumble means rearranging it into order, so these letters are rearranged into a real word

explanation.surface: A puzzled reader trying to understand the novelist Paul Gallico.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Gallico wrote The Snow Goose. 'Making sense of' rearranges the seven letters of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reasonable and coherent makes sense, the same idea as a rational, reasoned conclusion.

clue.text: The image of Holy Russia

parts.note: the painted religious images of saints venerated in Orthodox churches typify old Holy Russia

explanation.surface: A phrase evoking the very picture of old Orthodox Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious painting on wood used in Orthodox worship, emblematic of Holy Russia, also means any image or emblem.

clue.text: Somehow green and in charge of a class

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters come out in some other way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone inexperienced is oddly placed in charge of a school class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges GREEN into GENER. 'Class' here means a category, not a schoolroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a whole group or kind rather than an individual one, as in a genus or category.

clue.text: Finding faults with locks coming apart

definitions.meaning: drawing petty, overly fine distinctions in argument
locks are tresses of hair, and split ends literally divide strands

explanation.surface: Criticising something as damaged locks fall to pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' looks like door hardware; it means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Quibbling over trivial distinctions is a way of picking holes and carping, the pedant's fault-finding.

clue.text: Ends up with class displaying excessive neatness

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: tips are ends, as of fingers
and means with, joining two things
polish means refinement or class

explanation.surface: Something finishes up classy, showing a fussy tidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TIPS into SPIT, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from soldiers shining boots, and means scrupulous, sometimes overdone, smartness and cleaning.

clue.text: Loving the commotion and the band

parts.note: ado is fuss or commotion
a ring is a band, as worn on the finger

explanation.surface: Someone delights in the noisy fuss and in the musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like a group of musicians; it is a circlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing deep affection and devotion is a synonym for being fond in a tender, worshipful way.

clue.text: No child gets two points in set

indicators.note: in means the points sit inside the word for set

parts.note: a group is a set of things
W and N are two compass points, west and north

explanation.surface: A kid is given a couple of marks within a class set.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult is by definition no longer a child, so the phrase defines a mature person.

clue.text: Visitor hurries round to take in industrial Germany

indicators.note: round tells us to turn the found letters back to front
the phrase says the letters are taken in from within the clue's words, spanning their join

explanation.surface: A guest rushes about to see the sights of Germany's factory heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take in' finds RHUR across 'Visitor hurries'; 'round' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The valley of this river in western Germany is the country's historic coal and steel manufacturing district.

clue.text: Staff Sergeant initially given credit

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of the word Sergeant

parts.note: tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A staff sergeant is first given some credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like part of the rank; it is the definition. 'On tick' is British for on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a walking pole or rod, the same object as a cane or rod.

clue.text: Sort of saw for pine

definitions.meaning: a fine-bladed saw for cutting ornamental patterns in wood
to pine is to worry or grieve anxiously

explanation.surface: A kind of saw suited to cutting pine wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like timber for the saw; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A fretsaw cuts decorative woodwork, and to worry anxiously is to pine or brood.

clue.text: Game that is decided in the end

definitions.text: Game that is decided in the end

parts.words: Game that is decided in the end
parts.note: in the lawn game played on a green, each round of play is called an end

explanation.surface: A sport whose result is only settled at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: In this lawn game, played by rolling weighted balls toward a jack, each round of play is called an 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: The lawn game is scored end by end, so it is literally decided in the end.

clue.text: Ways out exist in conversion

indicators.note: something in conversion is being changed into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Escape routes are present in a building being converted.
explanation.definitionFit: Doors leading outside are the routes of departure, plain synonyms for egress points.

clue.text: Criticise girl who released much evil

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a critic pans a play
Dora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone is told to criticise a girl who has unleashed great wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth she opened a jar (a box in later tellings) and let loose the world's evils.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology the first woman opened a forbidden jar and let ills escape into the world.

clue.text: Dictionary the French team study

parts.note: le is French for the
XI is eleven, a football or cricket team
to con is an old word for studying or learning

explanation.surface: A French squad pores over a reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: A word list or vocabulary of a language is another name for a wordbook.

clue.text: You might be if a plan goes wrong

definitions.text: You might be if a plan goes wrong

indicators.note: when something goes wrong it is thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wry remark about how one feels when plans unravel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes wrong' rearranges the letters of 'if a plan'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agitated and panicky is how one feels when a scheme collapses, an everyday idiom for fluster.

clue.text: Prompt aid for those on TV

definitions.text: Prompt aid for those on TV

parts.words: Prompt aid for those on TV
parts.note: a screen device scrolling a script so presenters can read their lines while facing the camera

explanation.surface: A description of a quick help for television presenters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like an adjective meaning quick; it is a noun, a cue for words.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the trademark name for a teleprompter that displays a script to newsreaders and presenters.

clue.text: Pearl queasy, going to doctor in island capital

indicators.note: feeling queasy is being unsettled, so these letters are churned up

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: Pearl feels sick and goes to see a doctor in an island city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queasy' rearranges PEARL into PALER.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of Sicily, the largest island in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: New part ordered in foreign port

indicators.note: the letters are put in a fresh order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A replacement component is sent for from an overseas harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: The city on the Scheldt is Belgium's main seaport, a port overseas to a British solver.

clue.text: Defendant made charges

definitions.meaning: the person on trial in a criminal court
past tense of blaming someone formally, alleging wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A person on trial has levelled allegations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made charges' could be billing for goods; it is blaming.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner standing trial is so called, and the word is also the past tense of indict.

clue.text: Ruler and large sheet of paper required

definitions.meaning: a traditional British paper size, the biggest of the old drawing sheets

explanation.surface: A monarch needs a big sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruler' may suggest a measuring stick beside paper; it is a sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an empire is a sovereign, and the same name labels a very large old paper size.

clue.text: Small measures that ought to stimulate initially

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Small doses of drink that should perk you up from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small serving of spirits such as whisky or rum, a little measure.

clue.text: It may be used to lift obstruction

definitions.text: It may be used to lift
definitions.meaning: a pulley housing, as in the lifting gear called a tackle

explanation.surface: Something for hoisting away a barrier.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulley in a frame helps hoist loads, and a barrier or stoppage is also so called.

clue.text: Work by a pupil is a gem

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
L is the learner sign worn by British learner drivers

explanation.surface: A student's work is praised as a little treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupil' gives L, the British learner-driver plate letter, not a schoolchild.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky iridescent silica stone is prized as a precious stone in jewellery.

clue.text: Pure and simple French mother

definitions.meaning: the French word for mother, without its accent

explanation.surface: A description of a mother from France as wholesome and modest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nothing more than stated is being only or sheer, and mère is French for mother.

clue.text: Possibly hums something sentimental

indicators.note: possibly indicates one possible arrangement of the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone may be humming a soppy song.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloppy, cloying sentimentality is often called slush or soppiness, and this word too.

clue.text: An explosive type of reaction

parts.note: fission or fusion of atomic cores, the kind of reaction in atomic bombs

explanation.surface: Someone's furious response to some news.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an angry outburst; read literally it is atomic physics.
explanation.definitionFit: Fission chain reactions inside atoms power bombs, making atomic reactions literally explosive.

clue.text: Evens the score with bribes?

definitions.meaning: levels the match or settles accounts
to buy someone off, pay them to look away

explanation.surface: Someone settles a grudge by paying people off.
explanation.definitionFit: Levelling a game or account and paying someone off are both senses of the same verb.

clue.text: County present cars to rent

parts.note: here means present, as at a roll call
Fords are cars made by the Ford company
to hire is to rent

explanation.surface: A local authority offers vehicles for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a verb, to give; it means in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an English shire on the Welsh border, famous for cattle and cider.
